essay.title: PAPER I - ESSAY, COMPREHENSION & SUMMARY
essay.instruction: SECTION A: Answer one (1) composition question. SECTION B and SECTION C are compulsory. Theory score: 60 marks.

questions.question:
SECTION A — CONTINUOUS WRITING (30 MARKS)
You are dissatisfied with some practices in your school. Write a letter to your friend in another school discussing at least three of the practices and the improvements you desire.

Your answer should not be less than 450 words.

SECTION A — CONTINUOUS WRITING (30 MARKS)
Write an article for publication in a national newspaper on the high cost of living, suggesting at least three ways in which the government of your country can tackle the problem.

Your answer should not be less than 450 words.

SECTION A — CONTINUOUS WRITING (30 MARKS)
The Parent-Teacher Association of your school has decided to transform the school into a single-sex school. As the senior prefect, write a letter to the chairman, giving at least three reasons why you disagree with the decision.

Your answer should not be less than 450 words.

SECTION A — CONTINUOUS WRITING (30 MARKS)
You are the main speaker in a debate on the topic: "Children of literate parents perform better in school than those of illiterate parents." Write your argument for or against the motion.

Your answer should not be less than 450 words.

SECTION A — CONTINUOUS WRITING (30 MARKS)
Write a story that ends with the statement: "We apologized to each other and reconciled."

Your answer should not be less than 450 words.

SECTION B — COMPREHENSION (15 MARKS)

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions on it.

The success or failure of an organization depends largely on the head of such an organization. In any organization, whether big or small, people have to work together. The achievement of the goals or objectives of the organization makes it mandatory for teams to be formed. The moment a team is formed, there must be a head.

The head plays a very crucial role in helping the organization to realize its goals. It is the head that coordinates and harnesses the efforts of the team. His ability to harness the efforts of the team effectively and thus bring about the full realization of the objectives of the organization depends on his perception of himself. Does he see himself as a boss or a leader?

If the head sees himself as a boss, he would be a human hawk and his attitude to his teammates could best be summarized in one word: terrorism. The boss applies all sorts of techniques and tactics to make his subordinates do what he wants. He may resort to harassment, bullying, intimidation and coercion of his subordinates, all in the name of performing his role. Workers in such an organization are therefore always afraid of the boss and they dare not offer any advice or suggestion, however useful or sound it may be. There is a general atmosphere of frustration among workers. Of course, a frustrated worker cannot give of his best. In the final analysis, the organization suffers by not achieving most of the goals it set out to achieve.

On the other hand, if the head perceives himself as a leader, he treats his team members as human beings who deserve humane treatment and respect. He sees his subordinates as very important in the realization of the goals of the organization. He solicits their support and cooperation. He is persuasive rather than coercive. He makes his teammates see the rationale behind every action he takes and thus carries them along. A leader therefore promotes high morale among team members, high productivity and the full realization of the objectives of the organization. There is little wonder, then, why some organizations perform poorly while others perform well above expectations.

Answer the following questions:
(a) Why is it necessary for people to work together in an organization?
(b) What is the function of the head in an organization?
(c) How can the head of an organization become a "human hawk"?
(d) What can happen in the end if the head behaves merely as a boss?
(e) What will be the consequences for the organization if the head sees himself as a leader?
(f) In the question, "Does he see himself as a boss or a leader?", what literary device is used?
(g) In the expression, "If the head sees himself as a boss":
(i) What is the grammatical name given to the expression?
(ii) What is its function?
(h) For each of the following words, find another word or phrase that means the same and can replace it as used in the passage:
(i) mandatory
(ii) plays
(iii) realize
(iv) offer
(v) perceives
(vi) rationale.

SECTION C — SUMMARY (15 MARKS)

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

Theatre in the recent past used to be a very popular art in traditional African society. It used to be a point of intersection where members of the community not only came to entertain themselves but also shared communal fellowship.

Quite apart from that, in the traditional context, African drama and theatre were also popular and respectable institutions in that they preserved the people's culture and tradition. Theatre was popular with the people because it emphasized community participation, peace and progress. The presentations focused on the people's lives, their aspirations, fears and hopes. But today the situation is different. Theatre is becoming very unpopular.

Africa of the present age is preoccupied with many problems yearning for immediate solutions. The continent is facing hydra-headed challenges on the political, social and economic scenes. In a world where science and technology are seen as the solutions to these problems, little attention is paid to the arts. Literature generally, and drama in particular, is often rated low on the utility scale. Many in Africa today look at drama and theatre as mere forms of entertainment.

Elitism is another barrier that militates against the appreciation of theatre as a communal art. Folk theatre is appreciated by a negligible number of people. Contemporary focus is on literary theatre. Unfortunately, literary theatre only pretends to serve the interests of its society while, in reality, it often has a foreign audience in mind. The use of European and American theatrical conventions by African academic playwrights bears witness to this anomaly.

The popularity of literary African theatre is further marred by the medium of communication, as most literary dramas in Africa are written in foreign languages which are not understood by many Africans.

(a) In three sentences, one for each point, state three functions which theatre used to perform in traditional African society.
(b) In three sentences, one for each point, state three reasons given by the writer for the declining popularity of theatre in Africa.
